function: Graph-Transformer (G-TMUC) extrapolates the channels of L unknown nearby users from the known channels and locations of N users, cutting pilot overhead (pp. 1-4).
system: Multi-user massive MIMO: BS UPA with 20-120 antennas, multi-antenna users (20-120 in Fig. 5); sub-6 GHz and mmWave stated generically; no RIS (pp. 1, 4-5).
method: Supervised deep learning: 3-layer GIN graph encoder plus Transformer encoder-decoder (4 heads, 256-dimensional), trained with an NMSE loss against true channels (pp. 2-3).
data_channel: Wireless InSite ray-tracing data for training and test with Poisson-process and hotspot user locations; system model Saleh-Valenzuela; no public dataset named (pp. 1, 4).
test_conditions: Same ray-tracing generator for training and test; SNR 0-20 dB, 16-80 pilots and 20-120 user antennas swept; no unseen scenario or band tested (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: OMP. Learned: BNN (HMM prior for online estimation, matching ref. [8]) and NN (fully connected layers) (p. 4).
metrics: NMSE of the extrapolated channels versus SNR, number of pilots and number of user antennas; average user spectral efficiency (effective rate) versus SNR (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 4: "Training and test data are generated via ray-tracing (Wireless Insite)"; an own ray-tracing scene, not DeepMIMO or another named public dataset; the 3GPP TR 36.873 claim concerns the user distributions (see notes).
q2_support: p. 4: "Training and test data are generated via ray-tracing (Wireless Insite)"; Figs. 3-5 only sweep SNR, pilots and user antennas, and the paper never says a model trained on one setting is tested on another.
q3_support: p. 4: "OMP (sparse signal processing for channel recovery)" is the non-learned baseline; p. 4: "and (3) NN (fully-connected layers for" and the BNN are learned baselines, all compared on NMSE in Figs. 3-5.
q4_support: p. 3: "at higher computational cost" is only a qualitative remark on Transformer heads; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime is reported, and the 50% pilot reduction is signaling overhead.
q5_support: p. 4: "Training and test data are generated via ray-tracing (Wireless Insite)"; no code or data link or DOI is given and no public dataset is named.
notes: q1 is borderline: the data are Wireless InSite ray tracing in an unnamed scene (p. 4), and 3GPP TR 36.873 is named only as the standard that the user distributions and multi-scenario evaluation comply with ("3 GPP TR 36.873 for multi-scenario evaluation in urban deployments"); marked 0, reviewer to confirm (it would be 1 only if that claim is accepted as use of another standardized model). The system model (p. 1) names the Saleh-Valenzuela model, which does not count. Fig. 5 labels its sweep as user antennas, while the text on p. 4 gives the BS array as 20 to 120 antennas. The BNN baseline matches ref. [8], a Bayesian neural network.
